text:
Pranav: Quick thread — profiler shows p95/p99 skew coming from prefill after the kernel-swap last week. Raw numbers from today's canary: prefill p95=210ms p99=580ms, decode p95=95ms p99=180ms. Need to decide optimization order. cc @Sasha @Igor
Sasha: Those prefill p99 spikes line up with the KV cache miss pattern we saw. Example trace: `kv_cache.lookup miss -> fallback_full_attention_path` :eyes:
Igor: Confirmed. Flame profile shows repeated full-attention kernel runs during prefill for longer seqs. Kernel selection heuristic is choosing the unfused path at ~>768 tokens after the benchmark tweak. I think the threshold drifted.
Maya: If we fix the prefill kernel heuristic first we should shave a lot off the tail without touching batching. My back-of-envelope: kernel fix => p99 drops ~200–300ms on hot routes.
Sam: Alternative is adaptive microbatching + earlier KV prefetch. That can help throughput vs tail tradeoffs, but microbatching risks raising p50. Reminder: standard-tier SLO is 200ms p95 per-route.
Pranav: Proposed action order: (1) revert the kernel-threshold change in runtime->benchmarks branch, (2) implement a quick-path on KV miss to avoid falling into full-attention, (3) add KV-prefetch for prefix tokens on hot routes. Thoughts?
Sasha: Order 1,3,2 maybe. Revert is small and low-risk so we can measure impact quickly. But 3 (quick-path on miss) could give immediate decode savings; 2 (prefetch) depends on traffic heatmaps.
Igor: I vote 1 then 2 then 3. I can add a synthetic harness to measure impact: mix sequence lengths 256/512/1024, kv-miss ratio 40%, and microbatch sizes [1,4,8]. I'll push the harness and attach results. Example harness command we use:
```
./perf_harness --model r-infer-1 --seq-mix 256:50,512:30,1024:20 --kv-miss 0.4 --microbatches 1,4,8 --iters 2000
```
Maya: Also we _need_ per-token timing in prod logs split into prefill_time_ms and decode_time_ms. Right now we only have total token latency and it's hard to attribute regressions. Adding gauges + tracing spans will speed root-cause.
perf-bot: created alert: "prefill_p99 > 400ms for 10m" on dedicated-canary pool.
Sam: I'll run the canary after the revert. If we see prefill_p99 drop below 350ms, we can postpone more invasive changes.
Pranav: Thanks. I'll open the revert PR and a small metrics PR for prefill/decode splits (link in thread). Igor — please post harness artifacts and a short table of prefill vs decode time per microbatch size. Reconvene 1pm to review numbers. :thumbsup:
